title: A per-invocation hook pays a cold runtime start on every call, a resident process pays it once
claim: A delivery mechanism implemented as a hook that spawns a runtime per invocation costs two orders of magnitude more per call than the same work done inside a long-lived process, because the runtime start dominates and is paid every time.
appliesTo: Environment not reported by the submitter.
expectation: two mechanisms doing the same lookup over the same data cost about the same, so the choice between them is about reach rather than speed
reality: measured on the same corpus and the same query, a PreToolUse hook cost 130ms per tool call while an MCP proxy holding the index in memory cost 1-2ms, roughly 65x. The hook's cost is paid on every call whether or not anything matches, so an agent making a hundred tool calls spends about thirteen seconds waiting for, typically, zero warnings. Nothing in the hook was slow: node start plus bundle parse plus index build is the whole figure, and a resident process pays it once at connect.
workaround: Put delivery in a long-lived process wherever the protocol allows one, and keep per-invocation hooks only for the moment a resident process cannot reach — which for MCP is before the call rather than after it. Measure per-call rather than per-run: a benchmark that starts the process once hides exactly the cost that matters.

evidence.command: for i in 1 2 3; do time .claude/hooks/pre-tool-use.sh < event.json; done
evidence.note: The hook this timed, .claude/hooks/pre-tool-use.sh, was removed at commit 0dfe123 for the reason in BANK.md: its text reached the model alongside the result of the call it was about, not before the decision. The file is in git history at that commit's parent; the measurement stands as recorded.

evidence.command: bench.mjs: 20 calls through cairn-proxy vs direct upstream
evidence.output:
upstream direct   connect 209ms | per call: median 1ms  p95 5ms
through cairn-proxy connect 471ms | per call: median 2ms  p95 35ms

check.command: S=$(date +%s%N); node -e '' ; E=$(date +%s%N); MS=$(( (E-S)/1000000 )); echo "cold node start ${MS}ms"; [ "$MS" -gt 40 ]
check.confirmedIf: a bare runtime start alone exceeds 40ms, so any per-invocation hook inherits at least that
check.refutedIf: the runtime starts in under 40ms and the per-call penalty is negligible

observations.note: Recorded at the moment it was solved; no note was supplied.
